title: How a SCIP symbol string is read, and what reading it does not make it
why: A SCIP symbol string is a provider identifier. It is unique inside one index produced by one indexer at one package name and version, and it is not a universal identity for the node it points at: this index alone gives the module client.py two different strings, `dtcr-scip-fixture 1 client/__init__:` where it is defined and the same descriptor under a different package prefix where it is imported. Reading such a string as a cross-provider node id merges two nodes that were never compared. This file is the mediating rule the frozen symbol-fact schema demands beside every identifier, and its sha256 over the canonical form below is the scheme_digest each emitted identity carries. Change any mapping here and every identity emitted afterwards is under a different scheme, which is the point: the mapping is part of the identity, not a comment about it.

grammar.source: sourcegraph/scip scip.proto, the Symbol message's documented string syntax
grammar.local_symbol_form: local <simple-identifier>, scoped to one document and addressable from nowhere else
grammar.space_escape: a single space separates scheme, manager, package name and version; a double space is one literal space inside a token
grammar.name_escape: a name wrapped in backticks may hold any UTF-8; a doubled backtick is one literal backtick

resolution_classes.PROJECT_DEFINED: a SymbolInformation for this symbol exists in some document of this index
resolution_classes.EXTERNAL_DECLARED: no document defines it, but Index.external_symbols declares it
resolution_classes.DOCUMENT_LOCAL: a local <id> symbol, addressable only inside its own document
resolution_classes.UNRESOLVED_IN_INDEX: an occurrence names a symbol that neither a document nor external_symbols declares; the indexer saw the reference and did not carry its definition into this index

relationship_kind_from_occurrence.why_calls_is_absent: A SCIP occurrence records that a symbol appears at a range and, through symbol_roles, whether the appearance defines, imports, reads or writes it. None of those bits says a call happened: in this subject the identifier Client at pricing.py line 35 is a type annotation and the identifier format_total at line 40 is a call, and the index gives them the same read-access role. An importer that labelled either one CALLS would be reporting its own guess as the indexer's finding. CALLS is emitted only from a relationship the indexer itself resolved and marked, and this indexer emitted none.
relationship_kind_from_occurrence.why_lower_bound: The from-end of every edge here is the smallest enclosing_range the indexer attached to a definition occurrence that contains the reference. That attribution misses dynamic dispatch, reflection, callbacks, generated code and every reference the indexer did not resolve, so the edge set is a floor on what exists and never a ceiling.
